high_level_description: Strictly non-photographic, wordless Jura enamel-and-engraving illustration of a mechanical songbird automaton: a jammed motion advances a ratchet through three brass detents, the final detent engages a red brake and opens one fixed repair cradle, preventing endless attempts and making exhausted retry policy physically visible.

compositional_deconstruction.background: A Jura Arc watchmaking atelier has pale limewashed walls, one tall mullioned window and a grey stone floor beneath cool daylight. Fine copperplate contours and opaque enamel colors shape the scene in ivory, steel blue, brass, oxblood and black. No photograph, written dial, numeral, label, arrow, schematic line, book, tablet, textile panel, computer, brand mark, factory logo or national flag appears.

elements.desc: Large freestanding brass songbird automaton on an ivory enamel base, its cabinet open to reveal one spring drum, gear train, three-detent ratchet, red brake shoe and side repair cradle as parts of a single machine. The mechanism contains no clock face, numeral, written scale, arrow, wiring diagram, screen, brand, magical ornament or duplicate bird.

Single blue-enamel mechanical songbird mounted above the exposed gear train, with brass beak, steel wings and an oxblood tail. One wing gear rests visibly jammed against a bent feather-shaped cam while the bird leans forward without motion. It has no cage, crown, speech bubble, written tag, living plumage, glowing eye, duplicate body or separate control device.

Curved retry ratchet inside the automaton carrying exactly three round brass detents, two already displaced into shallow catch cups and the final detent pressed against an oxblood stop. That last contact clamps the red brake around the spring drum and mechanically releases the side repair cradle. No counted marks, digits, text, arrows, warning lamp or additional retry slot appears.

Fixed repair cradle unfolded from the automaton's right side, made from dark wood with an ivory felt lining and one red-edged hinge linked directly to the final brake. It waits to receive the stopped songbird mechanism rather than returning it to the drive. The cradle bears no label, cross symbol, arrow, document, spare bird, ranking badge or illuminated indicator.

Adult Jura watchmaker seated at the left workbench, light skin, short dark hair, plain steel-blue blouse, charcoal apron and round monocular loupe raised above one eye. With a patient neutral expression, both hands remain outside the stopped mechanism while observing the engaged brake; no gavel, crown, command staff, clipboard, written note, modern display or elevated chair appears.
